intro: Buying a home in Hawaii requires careful financial planning. High property prices, condominium association fees, insurance requirements and differences between island housing markets can all influence your monthly expenses.

Our free Hawaii mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment based on the purchase price, down payment, mortgage interest rate and repayment period. Include property taxes, homeowners insurance, hurricane coverage and applicable association fees to understand the financial commitment before purchasing a property.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Hawaii?

blocks.markdown:
An $840,000 Hawaii home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $4,028.98.

Here is an illustrative monthly housing payment breakdown.
This example assumes conventional financing without private mortgage insurance. Taxes, insurance, interest rates and association fees are illustrative rather than current statewide averages.

Hawaii's housing market varies significantly between islands and individual communities. Buyers can choose from condominiums in Honolulu, suburban properties on Oahu, homes on Maui and Kauai, and residential communities across the Island of Hawaii.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Hawaii housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/HI/POP715223), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $839,100 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $2,904, while the owner-occupied housing rate was 63%.

These historical statistics include existing homeowners who may have purchased their properties years earlier under different market conditions. They should not be interpreted as current mortgage quotes or average asking prices.

Compare recent property sales within your preferred island and neighborhood before selecting a purchase price for the calculator.

sections.heading: How to Use the Hawaii Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the expected purchase price of your property and your available down payment.

Select your preferred loan term and provide the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

Enter the property's annual tax liability, homeowners insurance premiums and other applicable insurance costs.

If you are purchasing a condominium, include its monthly maintenance or association fees. Add ground rent separately when budgeting for a leasehold property.

Include private mortgage insurance where required by your financing arrangement.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and amortization schedule. Adjust the home price or down payment to compare different purchase scenarios.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare Hawaii's financing costs with those in other states.

sections.heading: How Property Taxes Are Calculated in Hawaii

blocks.markdown:
Hawaii's real property taxes are administered at the county level. Tax classifications, rates and exemptions vary depending on the property's location and use.

A primary residence, investment property and short-term rental may have different tax classifications even when their assessed values are similar.

The [Honolulu Real Property Assessment Division's statewide reports](https://realproperty.honolulu.gov/statewide-reports/2026-27/) provide information about real property taxation across Hawaii's counties.

Use the relevant county's tax assessment records rather than applying one statewide effective tax rate.

### Honolulu home exemption

Eligible owner-occupants in the City and County of Honolulu can reduce their taxable assessed property value through the home exemption.

The [official Honolulu home exemption guidance](https://realproperty.honolulu.gov/tax-relief-and-forms/exemptions/home-exemption) lists the following amounts:

These exemptions reduce taxable assessed value rather than directly reducing your mortgage balance.

Eligibility depends on ownership, occupancy, filing requirements and other conditions.

### Hawaii property tax calculation example

Suppose you purchase a Honolulu property with an assessed value of $840,000 and qualify for the $120,000 home exemption applicable during the 2026–2027 tax year.

Your net taxable value would be $720,000.

Using an illustrative residential tax rate of $3.50 per $1,000 of taxable assessed value:

Annual property tax = $720,000 ÷ 1,000 × $3.50

The resulting annual tax would be $2,520, equivalent to $210 per month.

Actual property taxes depend on your county, tax classification, applicable rates and exemption approval.

Confirm those details with the local assessor before relying on the estimate.

Insurance requirements can differ across Hawaii because properties face varying environmental risks.

A standard homeowners insurance policy may not provide every type of coverage required by your lender or appropriate for the property's location.

### Hurricane insurance

The [Hawaii Department of Commerce and Consumer Affairs](https://cca.hawaii.gov/ins/prepare-for-hurricane-season/) advises homeowners that standard residential policies commonly exclude hurricane damage.

Separate hurricane coverage or an endorsement may therefore be necessary.

Obtain quotes for all required policies before estimating your total annual insurance cost.

Review applicable deductibles carefully, since a percentage-based deductible can create a considerable out-of-pocket expense following a covered loss.

### Flood and other environmental risks

Properties near coastal areas, rivers or low-lying locations may face flooding.

Check the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) and discuss appropriate coverage with your insurance agent.

Depending on the island and property location, volcanic activity, earthquakes and other hazards may also warrant additional investigation.

Do not assume that every natural hazard is covered by a standard insurance policy.

Condominiums are an important housing option for buyers in Honolulu and other densely developed areas.

Monthly maintenance fees can support shared facilities, elevators, building insurance, landscaping, security and common-area repairs.

These charges can substantially affect affordability.

Consider two properties with identical monthly principal and interest payments of $3,000. If one has monthly association fees of $350 and another has fees of $850, the second property costs an additional $500 per month before other expenses are considered.

Review the association's reserve study, financial statements, insurance arrangements and planned repairs.

Special assessments may require additional payments beyond ordinary monthly dues.

Your mortgage calculator estimate should include recurring association fees, but one-time assessments and unexpected repairs need separate consideration.

sections.heading: Fee Simple Versus Leasehold Properties in Hawaii

blocks.markdown:
Understanding the property's ownership structure is particularly important in Hawaii.

With fee simple ownership, the purchaser generally acquires ownership of the land and improvements, subject to applicable legal restrictions.

A leasehold purchase provides rights to use the property for a defined lease period while another party retains ownership of the underlying land.

Leasehold properties can have lower advertised purchase prices, but ground rent, lease expiration dates and rent renegotiation provisions can affect long-term costs.

Mortgage eligibility may also depend on the remaining lease duration.

Before purchasing a leasehold property, obtain the lease documents and confirm financing requirements with your lender. Do not compare fee simple and leasehold properties using purchase prices alone.

Eligible applicants may also investigate the [Department of Hawaiian Home Lands](https://dhhl.hawaii.gov/information-for-applicants/), which administers a distinct homestead leasing program with specific eligibility requirements.
These illustrations assume a 20% down payment, 6% fixed interest and a 30-year mortgage.

Taxes, insurance, association fees, ground rent and mortgage insurance are excluded.

Buyers considering expensive properties should check applicable county-specific conforming mortgage limits through the [Federal Housing Finance Agency](https://www.fhfa.gov/).

The Hawaii Housing Finance and Development Corporation, or HHFDC, administers financing initiatives for eligible residents.

### Hale Kamaʻāina Mortgage Program

The [Hale Kamaʻāina Mortgage Program](https://dbedt.hawaii.gov/hhfdc/2026/06/16/hale-kama%CA%BBaina-mortgage-program-for-homebuyers-frequently-asked-questions/) provides eligible first-time homebuyers with 30-year fixed-rate mortgage financing.

The program aims to offer interest rates below prevailing market levels, subject to funding and financing conditions.

Applicants must meet applicable residency, household income, property price and homebuyer education requirements.

The program's [eligibility and purchase price guidelines](https://dbedt.hawaii.gov/hhfdc/hale-kama%CA%BBaina-mortgage-program-eligibility-income-and-purchase-price-requirements/) include county-specific restrictions.

Confirm available funding and mortgage terms directly with an approved participating lender.

### Mortgage Credit Certificate program

Hawaii's [Mortgage Credit Certificate program](https://dbedt.hawaii.gov/hhfdc/current-mcc-holders-page/) previously provided eligible homeowners with federal income tax benefits.

HHFDC currently states that it is not accepting new MCC applications. Certain existing certificate holders may still qualify for reissuance when refinancing.

New buyers should not assume this tax benefit remains available for their purchase.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Hawaii?

blocks.markdown:
Evaluate your take-home income alongside housing expenses, groceries, transportation, utilities and regular savings contributions.

Island-specific shipping and maintenance costs can affect household budgets. Consider the cost of repairing or replacing major appliances and maintaining your property.

Use our [Hawaii Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/hawaii-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to understand existing borrowing obligations.

Review the [CFPB's homebuying guidance](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/) before accepting financing.

### How much is a mortgage payment on an $840,000 Hawaii home?

With 20% down, 6% fixed interest and a 30-year mortgage, principal and interest would be approximately $4,028.98 monthly. Taxes, insurance and association fees increase your total housing expenses.

### Does Hawaii have a statewide residential property tax rate?

No. Real property tax rates, classifications and exemptions vary by county. Obtain the applicable assessment and tax information from the county responsible for your property.

### Is first-time homebuyer mortgage assistance available in Hawaii?

Yes. Eligible buyers may investigate HHFDC's Hale Kamaʻāina Mortgage Program. Income limits, property price restrictions, residency requirements and funding availability apply.

Use our Hawaii mortgage calculator to compare financing scenarios and estimate your recurring housing expenses. Obtain accurate tax, insurance and association information before committing to a property, particularly when purchasing a condominium or leasehold home.
